short: A song or poem of mourning.
note: A lament, particularly a song or poem mourning someone’s death.
A comber is a long wave whose crest curls over and breaks.
A strong bluish-green color, also the name of the green chromium-based pigment used by painters.

short: Pale green or bluish green, like beryl.
note: Resembling beryl, especially the pale or bluish-green color of that mineral.

short: Matter inferred chiefly from gravitational effects.
note: Matter that does not emit, absorb, or reflect detectable light, but whose presence is inferred from its gravitational influence on galaxies and other cosmic structures. Its physical nature remains unresolved.
Ganesha is the Hindu god distinguished by an elephant’s head and a human body. He is associated with overcoming obstacles and is invoked at the beginning of undertakings.

short: Possibly Bobby Fischer, the American chess champion.
note: Possibly Bobby Fischer (1943–2008), the American chess player who defeated Boris Spassky in Reykjavík in 1972 to become world champion.

sources.label: World Chess Hall of Fame · Fischer–Spassky

short: Astronomical distance units of about 3.26 light-years.
note: A parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends one second of arc, approximately 3.26 light-years. Its name combines parallax and second.

short: Distances light travels in a year.
note: A light-year is a unit of distance: the distance light travels through a vacuum in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometers or 5.88 trillion miles.

short: Promote a pawn to a queen.
note: In chess, a pawn reaching the farthest rank must be exchanged for a queen, rook, bishop, or knight of the same color. Choosing a queen is called queening.

short: The decimal place-value system using digits 0–9.
note: Hindu-Arabic numerals use ten digits and position to express numbers. Developed in India and transmitted through Arabic mathematics, the system reached medieval Europe through translations and commercial arithmetic.

sources.label: University of St Andrews · Arabic numerals

short: A chess move expressed in descriptive notation.
note: In descriptive chess notation, files are named for the pieces that begin on them and ranks are counted from each player’s side. “Rook’s four” means the fourth square along a rook’s file.
